title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page belongs to the 'équation des lacets' sequel to La Longue Marche. There M = N_{1,1}^~ ≅ Γ_Q^~·SL(2,Z)^ is the group acting on the profinite fundamental group of the (1,1) situation, and Z^! ≅ M[0] is a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group of 'liftings'. On the previous page Grothendieck had a non-commutative central extension E of μ×μ by μ, with μ = {±1}. Since E_ab ≅ μ×μ, E is D4 or Q8. He asks what extension of Γ_Q by μ2 is induced by pulling back along Γ_Q → Gal(Q(ζ12)/Q) = (Z/12)^* ≅ (Z/3)^*×(Z/4)^* = μ×μ. That pulled-back extension is a class c ∈ H^2(Γ_Q, μ2) = Br(Q)[2].

On this page, hedged with 'sauf erreur en route', he proposes c = ξ'∪ξ''. Here ξ' and ξ'' are the Kummer classes in H^1(Q, μ2) = Q*/Q*^2 of the quadratic fields Q(√−3) = Q(ζ3) and Q(√3). Both lie in the biquadratic field Q(i, j) = Q(ζ12), whose third quadratic subfield is Q(i), 'le troisième larron'. He expects it to be 'trivial for a connoisseur of the foundations' that c ≠ 0, and suggests something even simpler involving Q(i).

In modern terms this is the classical embedding problem: does Q(ζ12)/Q embed into a D4/Q8 Galois extension, i.e. does the inflated class vanish? The obstruction is a quaternion-algebra class (a,b) ∈ Br_2(Q), computable by Hilbert symbols (Witt's theorems).

Second part, (116)–(117): he considers the central embedding of μ into S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} = Z^!_{ρ,σ} ×_γ N*_ρ ×_γ N*_σ, given by ε ↦ (1, ε, 1). This is a fibre product over γ ≅ Γ_Q of the GT-like group with the stabilizers N*_ρ, N*_σ of the torsion elements ρ, σ (up to the characters ε_3, ε_2). The image lies in the kernel L_ρ × L_σ of the projection to Z^!. Passing to the quotient gives a canonical 'lifting' homomorphism M[0] ≅ Z^! ≅ S_0^ΠΓ^!/μ → S_0Γ^!/i(μ). The next page makes this explicit via the two fundamental loops a, b (the 'équation des lacets'), with defining congruences in the profinite groups Π^, Π_0^.

So the page serves the question of whether the μ2-extension attached to the sign ambiguity in the loop a is split. It does so by first detecting it arithmetically on Γ_Q, then setting up the canonical section modulo μ.
errors: Cohomological degree slips. On the previous page c is written in H^1(Spec Q, μ2) ⊂ Br(Q); on this page ξ', ξ'' are written in H^2(Q, μ2). It should be c ∈ H^2(Q, μ2) = Br(Q)[2] and ξ', ξ'' ∈ H^1(Q, μ2) = Q*/Q*^2 (Kummer classes of quadratic extensions).

Substantive problem with the proposed formula. ξ'∪ξ'' = (−3)∪(3) = (−3,3), and (a,−a) = 0 for every a (the quaternion algebra (a,−a) is split). Hence with the stated choice c = 0, contradicting the expected c ≠ 0. Ironically, every other product of two of the classes (−1), (3), (−3) (including squares) is nonzero in Br(Q): e.g. (−1,−3) and (−1,3) are ramified at 3, and (−1,−1) at 2 and ∞. So either the identification of ξ', ξ'' is wrong (the hedge 'sauf erreur' is warranted), or the extension class of E is not simply χ_{−3}·χ_3 in H^2((Z/2)^2, Z/2).

The extension class in H^2(μ×μ, μ2) for a non-abelian E must involve the mixed term xy. The resulting Brauer class should be computed via Witt's criteria for D4/Q8 embedding problems; the page does not do this.

ideas.what: Identify the μ2-extension of Γ_Q induced by a central extension of Gal(Q(ζ12)/Q) ≅ (Z/2)^2 as a cup product of Kummer classes in Br_2(Q)
ideas.modern_name: Galois embedding problem for D4/Q8 over a biquadratic field; obstruction as quaternion algebra class (Witt, Serre-type cup-product formulas)

ideas.what: Central μ-embedding into fibre product Z^! ×_Γ N*_ρ ×_Γ N*_σ and canonical lifting homomorphism M[0] → S_0Γ^!/μ
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group acting on profinite SL(2,Z)/Γ_{1,1}; liftings via stabilizers of torsion elements (cf. Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura on GT and genus-1)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (1981)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a computation-in-progress inside Grothendieck's unpublished GT/loop-equation framework. The arithmetic part is a classical embedding-problem/Hilbert-symbol question, and the explicit proposed formula actually gives 0 because (3,−3) = 0. The structural part is set-up notation, made explicit on the next page. No new result or connection beyond the known GT/genus-1 literature.
transcription_corrections: 'H^2(Q, [-μ_?-] μ_2)' for ξ', ξ'': the image shows H^2 with a struck-over coefficient; mathematically H^1(Q, μ2) is meant.
'le μ-groupement central' is likely 'le μ-plongement central' (central μ-embedding).
'pour un connaisseur pour les fondements' is probably 'pour un connaisseur des fondements'.
